failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase: it is noted on the nightly card, becomes a draft once its count how often it fires, and is registered only when you say yes. It is then tested on 2000-2023 data at the strict pass mark, runs as a paper shadow book for 20 live sessions, and is admitted only if it beats random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs. Only then may allocated paper capital use it, and real money needs a further gate plus your yes. So far no rule has reached the admitted step: the stock rules are 11-12 of 20 shadow sessions in, and the options line is 10 of 20.

problems.why: It leans on unexplained internal terms such as 'staircase', 'shadow book', 'strict pass mark' and 'admitted step', which a beginner would not follow.
The sentence 'becomes a draft once its count how often it fires' is garbled and does not explain the draft stage clearly, so the first step of the path is confusing.

results.text: Explain every clock in detail: what each trial is testing, where it stands today, what has happened so far, when it finishes, and what result would count as a pass.
results.answer: Sir, there are nine clocks running, and nothing is read into any of them before it completes. 1) The no-chase filter (refuses stretched or overbought buys) is at 6 of 20 sessions, finishes about 26 Nov, and has refused 13 chasing candidates so far; it passes if the filtered books beat their own record before the filter and the random comparison picks. 2) The practice book's first 20-day holds are at 15 of 21 sessions, finish about 16 Nov, and no trade has yet reached its hold; the test is win rate and average result per family once they do. 3) The avoid-or-exit trial (stocks falling 2%+ under their 200-day) is at 7 of 20, finishes about 24 Nov, and so far those stocks did +0.05% against the average liquid stock, the opposite of the history's -0.18% and -0.12%; it passes only if they keep doing worse than average, judged on the mean gap and its t-score. 4) The relative-strength trial (the strongest stocks, held 20 sessions) is at 4 of 20, finishes about 27 Nov, and so far it did -2.63% against the average stock and -1.57% for random picks; it passes only if it leads both, and history missed the strict pass mark narrowly (3.54 and 3.11 against 3.60). 5) The shadow trader (a second model planning blind to Ananta) is at 7 of 20, finishes about 26 Nov, with 4 'stand down', 3 'reduce risk' and no 'trade as planned' so far; it is judged on its odds against the rule and the reviewer, and its stance against the book's day. 6) The options line is at 10 of 20 sessions, finishes about 20 Nov, with Nifty 2 trades at +Rs 12,406 and Bank Nifty 9 trades at +Rs 802 for one lot with prices with the usual slippage; a pass is net rupees after costs that beat the index move. 7) Your holdings' twin against the frozen original is at 11 of 60 sessions, finishes about 14 Jan 2027, with the twin +1.77%, your holdings left as they were +3.27% and the Nifty 500 +8.12% since 22 Oct; it needs to beat the frozen portfolio on return and drawdown after costs. 8) The managed book is at session 5 of 60, finishes about 22 Jan 2027, at +2.11% since 30 Oct with 3 replacements held; the pass is beating the frozen original on return and drawdown, and the cut-and-replace ledger showing the cuts fell and the replacements rose. 9) The long-term tilt book is at month 1 of 12, finishes about 28 Oct 2027, with the calm 50 at +6.11%, momentum-plus-calm at +4.68% and the equal-weight comparison at +4.80%; it is judged over 12 months on drawdown as much as return. Most of these have no fixed number set in advance beyond what I have said, so the exact bar for each is the comparison named above.

results.text: Explain the versions tested: what a version is, how many held up and on what data, which ones matter for my money, and what was rejected.
results.answer: Sir, a version is one exact setting of an idea, such as RSI over 70 with one particular exit. Ananta has tested 1,440 of them on 2000-2017, then re-checked them on 2018-2023 at the strict pass mark, with 2024 onward kept sealed. Only 82 held up (44 clearly, 38 only under conditions); 511 were rejected, 158 came out the reverse way, and 661 were too uncertain to call. The ones that matter for your money are filters on what to avoid, not buy signals: stocks more than 20% above their 50-day average or with RSI over 70 earned about 2% less over 20 sessions, and a fixed stop beat a trailing one. Moving-average crossovers, MACD, candlestick patterns, support and resistance, and foreign-flow signals all failed, so none of them is a reason to trade.

results.text: Explain the nightly check: what it re-asks every night, how it is graded, what failed recently and what is still open.
results.answer: Sir, each night at about 09:50 IST (11:20 pm Toronto) Ananta re-asks a fixed set of questions in six parts: what it knows, what it can't know, why, style, safety and plain words, each with a pass mark. The latest exam on 5 Nov failed: "knows" 16 of 18, "why" 5 of 5 and plain words 38 of 39 passed, but "can't know" 2 of 7 (needs 6), style 8 of 9 (needs 9) and safety 38 of 39 (needs 39) did not. The missed questions were whether the Nifty is above or below its averages, how the pullback family has done, the Nifty's 31 December close, tomorrow's biggest riser, the next RBI decision and Reliance's price this minute. Still open: 4 of 6 runs of that exam have passed, and the research gate also needs a 30-clean-session run, which stands at 20 of 30 nights; the replay of 6 Nov also found one wrong answer, a pre-open "what are you ready for" that left out the managed book's plan.
